summary: Monthly co-sell pipeline review between Redwood and TideWave. Reviewed three priority joint opportunities, discussed deployment preferences (hosted vs dedicated), compliance asks for EMEA customers, and action items to run benchmarks and share enablement materials. Agreed to schedule deeper technical session and to formalize joint account list.
topics: Deployment model tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Security/compliance asks for EMEA prospects (SOC2, KMS, data residency)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — um, we'll keep this tight, 45-ish minutes, quick pipeline review. Can folks intro themselves?
[00:12] Alicia (TideWave): Hi all, Alicia here, Head of Partnerships at TideWave. Liam's on for sales, Priya on solutions.
[00:18] Liam (TideWave): Hey team.
[00:20] Priya (TideWave SA): Hi.
[00:22] Maya (Redwood SE): Maya, Redwood SE — I'll lead the tech bits.
[00:26] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: top 3 joint deals, any blockers, security asks, then next steps. Ethan and Sofia from Redwood ops will chime in.
[01:05] Jordan: First deal is AcuTherm — you flagged them as high priority, Alicia?
[01:12] Alicia: Yep, AcuTherm is healthcare analytics, EMEA footprint, concern about data residency and audit logs, they want on-prem or VPC. They asked about SOC2 and our KMS integrations, and also want to understand SSO.
[01:28] Maya: Right, technically we have private deployment options — Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM support, and audit logs. There's a small lift for networking but we can scope it. Quick note: our on-prem packaging is more heavyweight but doable.
[01:45] Priya: How much of a perf hit do we see with Private vs Hosted? They care about latency for real-time clinical alerts.
[01:53] Maya: Good question. Hosted usually has lowest latency for small models — but for predictable throughput Dedicated pools are best. Private can be optimized similar to Dedicated if deployed with the right GPUs and kernel builds; we usually recommend benchmarking with a sample prompt set.
[02:12] Jordan: So action: Maya will run a benchmark plan for AcuTherm-like workloads.
[02:20] Alicia: Timeline? They want numbers this month.
[02:22] Maya: We can run an initial perf pass by next week if you can share sample prompts and target latency percentiles. I'll need sequence lengths and concurrency targets.
[02:34] Liam: I'll pull that into the sheet.
[03:10] Jordan: Deal two is Meridian Logistics — they're more SaaS, US+EMEA, small budgets, they asked about cost controls and fallbacks if capacity is constrained.
[03:22] Maya: For cost controls, Redwood has batching and quantization profiles; also smart routing so you can route to cheaper model variants during off-peak or have automatic fallbacks to lower-cost variants. You can set per-route policies.
[03:38] Priya: Do you have per-route quotas and token-level cost breakdowns for reporting?
[03:44] Sofia (Redwood CSM): Yes, Console shows per-route token usage, cost, and latency. We can export a monthly report for finance.
[04:05] Alicia: Any competitors in their corners? Meridian was evaluating Databricks and an MLOps play from another vendor.
[04:12] Jordan: Noted — Databricks and Cohere mentioned. We'll emphasize predictable throughput and lower unit cost on typical convo loads.
[04:30] [05:01] Jordan: Deal three — SummitRetail, they want a quick pilot, 6-week POC, focus on embeddings for search, and ask about embedding pipelines and vector DBs.
[05:12] Maya: On embeddings, we integrate with popular vector DBs; we also have embeddings endpoints with configurable dimensions and stability settings. For pilot, hosted is fastest to start, then migrate to Dedicated if volume grows.
[05:27] Priya: For pilot we need data retention settings and contract language — any standard doc?
[05:33] Jordan: We'll share a standard SOC2 + DPA package and sample SOW for a 6-week pilot.
[06:02] Liam: Quick question on co-sell motions — how do we formalize introductions? Month-to-month or do we want a joint account plan?
[06:10] Jordan: We prefer a joint account plan per top deal — TideWave identifies the contact at buyer org, Redwood AE owns the technical and commercial touchpoints, and partner lead coordinates customer intimacy. We'll put a pipeline spreadsheet in the partner portal.
[06:35] Alicia: Sounds good. Also, for EMEA deals we need data residency confirmation in writing — can you point to regions or partners who can support EU-only hosting?
[06:46] Maya: We have EU-hosted regions and can set up Dedicated capacity there; for Private we can do on-prem or a VPC in a customer-specified region. We'll include region notes in the doc we send.
[07:15] Jordan: Okay, now blockers — any legal/procurement timing concerns?
[07:22] Priya: SummitRetail has procurement windows that lock on the 15th of each month; they prefer shorter SOWs and clear exit criteria.
[07:30] Jordan: We'll prepare a tight SOW template.
[08:01] [08:45] Maya: A technical note — for low-latency clinical alerts (AcuTherm) we recommend packing KV cache and enabling continuous batching carefully; also consider quantization options that preserve accuracy, e.g., 4-bit QAT profiles we recently validated.
[09:05] Priya: Is QAT available in Private deployments?
[09:10] Maya: Yes, with the right runtime builds; it's part of the Dedicated/Private config options. There's an engineering lead time for custom kernel builds but it's manageable.
[09:35] Alicia: On the commercial side, how do we split co-sell credit? Revenue recognition and attribution are important to TideWave.
[09:42] Jordan: We usually do an attribution agreement per deal — partner introduction % and joint pipeline credits. Ethan will send sample partner MOU language.
[10:05] Ethan (Partner Ops): I'll drop a template in the portal after the call.
[10:20] [11:00] Liam: For Meridian, their main ask is a predictable TCO at scale — any example case studies?
[11:10] Sofia: We have a TCO brief for a similar logistics customer — I'll share that and token cost breakdowns per model.
[11:22] Jordan: We'll highlight batching/caching impact on unit cost and show options (hosted for speed, dedicated for predictability).
[11:50] Priya: About security — AcuTherm needs SOC2 plus country-level data residency and wants an audit log export on demand. Do you support syslog or S3 exports?
[12:02] Maya: Audit logs can be exported to customer S3 or splunk via syslog; the Private control plane offers full auditability.
[12:18] Alicia: Great. Also, are there any compliance certificates that TideWave can reference in proposals?
[12:24] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 Type II report and our DPA; also a note on encryption at rest with KMS and TLS in transit.
[12:40] [14:10] Priya: For the benchmark, what telemetry will you provide? Token latency percentiles, p95, p99, cost per 1M tokens?
[14:22] Maya: Yes we'll provide p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput numbers, and cost per token estimates under different batch/seq settings. We'll include the exact model variants used.
[14:33] Liam: Any guidance on model selection? Customer wants the best accuracy but budget-limited.
[14:39] Maya: We'll recommend a model family per workload — for retrieval-augmented search embeddings use our embedding v2, for chat use a mid-sized gen model with quantization. We'll share tradeoff matrix.
[15:05] Jordan: Quick logistics — I'll upload the co-sell pipeline spreadsheet to the partner portal after this call; please populate contacts and deal values. We'll also track close dates.
[15:18] Alicia: We'll add contacts today.
[15:24] [17:00] Jordan: Any legal hold ups? No. Procurement windows: SummitRetail — get SOW in by Dec 1 to make December cycle.
[17:12] Priya: Noted.
[17:35] Jordan: Final checklist: Maya runs perf, Jordan sends deck and sheet, Ethan sends partner MOU, TideWave identifies top 3 deals.
[18:05] Alicia: Thanks all.
[18:20] Jordan: We'll reconvene in two weeks or earlier if the benchmark uncovers anything.
[18:35] Maya: Scheduling note — technical deep dive tentatively week of Dec 7.
[18:50] Jordan: Great. End call.
[19:00] [End of recording]
